name: Overnight-intraday reversal (tug of war): firm-level overnight vs intraday return reversal
author_year: Lou, Polk and Skouras (2019, Journal of Financial Economics 134(1):192-213)
instrument: US individual stocks in the paper (universe not verified in accessible text) [uncertain]. No index, futures or CFD adaptation in the paper. Maven MT5 mapping: none.
timeframe: Daily: overnight component (prior close to today's open) and intraday component (open to close)
entry_rule: [uncertain] Paper constructs cross-sectional long-short portfolios from firm-level overnight and intraday return signals. Exact signal construction not read. Index adaptation would need a single-asset rule: trade the component that the prior-period sign points to [uncertain].
exit_rule: Overnight component: exit at next open. Intraday component: exit at close. [uncertain] for exact timing in the paper.
holding_time: Overnight leg about 16 hours (close to open); intraday leg about 6.5 hours (open to close)
trades_per_year: [uncertain] Up to about 250 per leg per instrument per year for a single index; the paper's portfolio counts not read.
overnight_weekend: Yes. Overnight leg holds through every close-to-open gap, including weekends if held over a Friday close [uncertain].
signal_window_definition: Overnight return = prior close to today's open; intraday return = open to close. DST handling not discussed in accessible sources [uncertain].
sample_period: [uncertain] Not read. Paper uses US stock data (JEL N22 suggests US) [uncertain].
out_of_sample: No explicit out-of-sample test confirmed in accessible text. The paper states persistence 'for years' [uncertain].
cost_assumption: [uncertain] Not stated in accessible sources. Paper says profits are earned entirely in one component, which makes cost treatment decisive; not verified.
reported_metrics: Qualitative only from abstract: strong overnight and intraday firm-level continuation with an offsetting cross-period reversal; across 14 strategies, profits are earned entirely overnight or entirely intraday, usually with opposite signs. No Sharpe or returns retrieved [uncertain].
third_party_replication: Not found for stocks. Related lead: 'The night effect of intraday trading: Chinese gold and silver futures markets' (Global Finance Journal 2025, ideas.repec) appeared in search but was not read [uncertain].
decay_status: [uncertain] Paper says the reversal lasts for years. Post-2019 decay not assessed. Same authors' 2026 FMG discussion paper (DP961) extends to equity premium; not read.
data_source_requirement: Daily open and close per instrument. For index/CFD adaptation: session open and close prices from Maven MT5 or Dukascopy (available in principle) [uncertain]. No options, VIX, TICK or funding needed.
min_lot_fit_5k10k: [uncertain] Not computable: no stop defined; overnight gap size per index unknown. Overnight holding means full gap risk on a 5K/10K account even at 0.01 lot.
fn_rule_fit: [uncertain] Overnight holding exposes the account to gap risk across Asia/Europe opens and overnight news; FN +-5 min 40% news rule not directly triggered by a close-to-open hold, but FN overnight/weekend policy not verified.
bot_policy_compliance: Rule-based and bot-compatible in principle; overnight holding needs a scheduler at close and open. FN overnight policy not verified [uncertain].
event_overlap: Overnight leg spans the Asian and European opens and overnight macro releases; intraday leg contains the US 08:30 ET release for US indices. Not quantified [uncertain].
overlap_with_existing: Not measured [uncertain]. Overnight-hold logic is partly related to the rejected BTC NYSE overnight long, but on a different instrument and rule set.
rejected_catalog_hit: PARTIAL: btc_nyse_overnight_long (rejected) is an overnight-hold long on BTC only; its scope excludes this idea. The 'reversal' search hit fx_fix_reversal_london_tokyo is a different mechanism. No overnight-intraday reversal entry found. Confirm with: python -m intraday.elenenler --kontrol overnight
base_rate_check: [uncertain] Return-continuation and reversal claims need a base rate of up-days versus down-days; paper magnitudes not read, so the claim cannot be checked against base rate yet.
pitfall_risk: High. Stock-level cross-sectional signal does not carry to a single index (index adaptation loses the cross-section); overnight gap cost and risk; 14-strategy search raises multiple-testing risk; cost treatment not verified.
